blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At finalized Ethereum block 26505987 (2026-11-27T10:37:11Z, hash 0x2b4fdfa8d374fad9409afe381d9e555acc8af9cfe407080de32e0506a4928cbb) and Tron block 88367386 (2026-11-27T10:47:18Z), both verified Paxos-derived XAUHImplementation deployments expose freeze(address), unfreeze(address), wipeFrozenAddress(address), and pause(). Because assetProtectionRole() currently returns the zero address on both chains, no active operator can freeze addresses directly today; however, the active 3-of-4 owner multisig (Safe 0xcfdb103596d55a9c896093ea5c49280c2e3e123b on Ethereum; native multisig TQjfg49gLwMEYWaG3gX9r32kXDJxEoW6iM on Tron) can call setAssetProtectionRole(address) with zero delay to grant an operator and activate address freezing and balance wiping. Under Pharos's FreezeWatch ladder, granting a blacklist operator first classifies as Possible rather than Yes. Terms section 8.5 also reserves freeze, blacklist, and legal confiscation powers. Ethereum (4,109.2 XAUH) and Tron (3,179.4 XAUH) account for 68.51% of the 10,638.9898 XAUH measured on-chain across Ethereum, TON, and Tron (and 47.02% of the 15,500 reported circulating total), well above the 10% materiality threshold. Event topics match the PAXG V1 family: AddressFrozen(address) 0x90811a8edd3b3c17eeaefffc17f639cc69145d41a359c9843994dc2538203690, AddressUnfrozen(address) 0xc3776b472ebf54114339eec9e4dc924e7ce307a97f5c1ee72b6d474e6e5e8b7c, FrozenAddressWiped(address) 0xfc5960f1c5a5d2b60f031bf534af053b1bf7d9881989afaeb8b1d164db23aede.
